message.content:
Below is a **complete example** of how you would create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If the RTX A6000 is not yet offered in your region, you can replace it with the next‑best GPU type, e.g. `nvidia-tesla-a100`.)

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Step | What to do |
|------|------------|
| 1 | **Enable the Compute Engine API** in your project. |
| 2 | **Set up billing** for the project. |
| 3 | **Create a service account** (or use your own credentials) with the following scopes: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. |
| 4 | **Install the Cloud SDK** (`gcloud`) if you haven’t already. |
| 5 | **Choose a zone** that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`). |

> **Tip:** You can list all zones that support GPUs with:
> ```bash
> gcloud compute zones list --filter="supportsAccelerators:true"
> ```

---

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
BOOT_DISK_SIZE="50GB"
BOOT_DISK_TYPE="pd-ssd"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size="$BOOT_DISK_SIZE" \
  --boot-disk-type="$BOOT_DISK_TYPE" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=./startup.sh   # optional
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | GPU type and count. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS). |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Size & performance of the boot disk. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that runs on first boot (e.g., to install NVIDIA drivers). |

> **Important:** After the instance starts, you’ll need to install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit manually or via a startup script. Google Cloud provides a [GPU driver installer](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus/install-drivers-gpu) that you can run automatically.

---

## 3. Using the REST API

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly, here’s a sample `POST` request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values.  
The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver automatically when the instance boots.

---

## 4. Verifying the Instance

After creation, you can verify that the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```json
"accelerators": [
  {
    "acceleratorCount": 1,
    "acceleratorType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
  }
]
```

---

## 5. Common Pitfalls & Tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU type not available in zone** | Check supported zones with `gcloud compute zones list --filter="supportsAccelerators:true"`. |
| **Billing not enabled** | Enable billing in the Cloud Console or via `gcloud beta billing projects link`. |
| **Driver not installed** | Use the startup script or SSH into the instance and run the NVIDIA driver installer. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Inspect the serial console logs via the Cloud Console or `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`. |

---

### Quick Summary

1. **Enable APIs & Billing** → **Choose a GPU‑capable zone** → **Create instance** (CLI or REST) → **Install drivers** → **Verify**.

Feel free to adapt the machine type, GPU count, or disk size to match your workload. Happy computing!
